# Team pack — generated by `pack init`

This directory is a Git-committed capability pack. It does not modify DeepSeek
Harness runtime packages.

## Layout

| Path | Role | Commit? |
|---|---|---|
| `composition.json` | Human-authored intent: units, patch layers, profile, bindings | yes |
| `pack.lock.json` | Generated content digests + capability closure | yes |
| `units/<id>/unit.json` | One unit manifest per distributable capability | yes |
| `units/<id>/…` | The files a unit ships (skills, commands, MCP config, scripts) | yes |
| `patches/*.patch.yml` | Ordered Cordis patch layers | yes |
| `README.md` | This file | yes |
| `.gitignore` | Keeps local credential values out of the repository | yes |

## Commands

Run `dsh-pack` from anywhere after the global shim is installed:

```sh
dsh-pack validate   --repo <this-dir>
dsh-pack sync       --repo <this-dir>
dsh-pack lock       --repo <this-dir>
dsh-pack verify     --repo <this-dir>
dsh-pack doctor     --repo <this-dir>
dsh-pack materialize --repo <this-dir> --home ~/.dsh
```

`sync` recomputes `unit.json.integrity.digest` from each unit's declared
`contents.sources` (sorted paths, CRLF→LF normalized bytes). Run it after
editing a unit's files, then run `lock`. `verify` fails on any byte-level drift
in a unit, on any hidden Unicode character, and on any mismatch with the
committed `pack.lock.json`.

## Distribute to a colleague

1. Colleague clones this repository.
2. `dsh-pack verify --repo <clone>` proves the clone matches the committed lock.
3. `dsh-pack doctor --repo <clone>` lists required credential **names**; the
   colleague supplies values locally. Values are never committed, read, or logged.
4. `dsh-pack materialize --repo <clone> --home ~/.dsh` writes the profile skeleton.
5. `dsh plugin --profile team add <spec>` installs the unit packages; then
   `dsh --profile team` boots it.

The profile directory itself stays outside Git. Only this pack is the team asset.
